NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION**

1.1 In this Contract, unless the context otherwise requires:
   - "Business Day" means any day (other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday) on which banks are open for general business in Lagos, Nigeria.
   - "Buyer's Premises" means the Buyer's restaurant locations as listed in Schedule A, or such other locations as the Buyer may designate in writing from time to time.
   - "Confidential Information" has the meaning set out in Clause 12.
   - "Force Majeure Event" has the meaning set out in Clause 13.
   - "Goods" means the fresh produce categories listed in Schedule B, as may be updated by written agreement of the Parties.
   - "Specifications" means the quality, grading, and packaging standards for the Goods as set out in Schedule C.

1.2 Headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Contract.

1.3 Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender include all genders.

**2. SUPPLY OF GOODS**

2.1 The Supplier shall supply, and the Buyer shall purchase, the Goods in accordance with the terms of this Contract.

2.2 The Supplier shall deliver the Goods to the Buyer's Premises in accordance with the delivery schedule set out in Schedule D, or as otherwise instructed by the Buyer via purchase orders.

2.3 Each delivery of Goods shall be accompanied by a delivery note specifying the date, time, quantity, and description of the Goods delivered.

**3. QUALITY AND SPECIFICATIONS**

3.1 The Supplier warrants that all Goods supplied under this Contract shall:
   - conform to the Specifications;
   - be of merchantable quality and fit for the purpose for which they are intended;
   - be free from defects, pests, and contamination; and
   - comply with all applicable laws and regulations of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

3.2 The Buyer may reject any Goods that do not conform to the Specifications within 24 hours of delivery. Rejected Goods shall be replaced by the Supplier at no cost to the Buyer within 48 hours of notification.

The Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 states its has_effective_date as 2024-01-15. Record status: historical.

**4. PRICE AND PAYMENT**

4.1 The price for the Goods shall be as set out in Schedule E, which shall remain fixed for the first six (6) months of this Contract.

4.2 Thereafter, prices may be adjusted by mutual written agreement of the Parties, with at least thirty (30) days' prior notice.

4.3 The Buyer shall pay all undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of the date of the invoice, by bank transfer to the Supplier's designated bank account.

4.4 The Buyer may withhold payment for any disputed amounts pending resolution.

**5. DELIVERY AND RISK**

5.1 Delivery of the Goods shall be deemed complete upon the Buyer's receipt and acceptance of the Goods at the Buyer's Premises.

5.2 Risk of loss or damage to the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery.

5.3 Title to the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon full payment for the Goods.

**6. PENALTY FOR LATE DELIVERY**

6.1 If the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods by the agreed delivery date or time, the Supplier shall pay to the Buyer a penalty of 0.05 (five percent) of the value of the undelivered Goods for each day of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the total value of the delayed order.
8.1 Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Contract (other than any payment obligation) to the extent that such failure or delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event.

8.2 For the purposes of this Contract, a "Force Majeure Event" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party, including but not limited to:
   (a) acts of God, flood, drought, earthquake, or other natural disaster;
   (b) epidemic or pandemic;
   (c) act of terrorism, civil unrest, riot, or war;
   (d) fire, explosion, or accident;
   (e) strikes, industrial disputes, or lockouts (other than those affecting the affected Party's own employees);
   (f) any law, regulation, or order of any governmental or regulatory authority; or
   (g) interruption or failure of utilities or transportation networks.

8.3 The affected Party shall promptly notify the other Party in writing of the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event and shall provide reasonable details of the nature and expected duration of the event. The affected Party shall use reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable.

8.4 If a Force Majeure Event continues for a period of more than thirty (30) consecutive days, either Party may terminate this Contract by written notice to the other Party. Such termination shall take effect fourteen (14) days after the date of the notice, unless performance of the affected obligations has resumed before such date.

**9. RENEWAL**

9.1 This Contract may be renewed for successive periods of twelve (12) months each (each a "Renewal Period") by mutual written agreement of the Parties, signed by their duly authorised representatives.

9.2 Any renewal shall be agreed no later than sixty (60) days prior to the Expiry Date. If the Parties do not agree to a renewal in accordance with this Clause 9, this Contract shall expire automatically on the Expiry Date without any further liability on either Party.

9.3 The terms and conditions of this Contract shall apply to any Renewal Period, unless the Parties agree in writing to amend such terms.

According to the contract, the Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 has_expiry_date is 2026-12-31. Record status: current.

**10. NOTICES**

10.1 Any notice required or permitted to be given under this Contract shall be in writing and shall be delivered personally, sent by registered post, or sent by email to the address of the relevant Party set out in Schedule A (or to such other address as a Party may notify to the other Party in writing from time to time).

10.2 A notice shall be deemed to have been received:
   (a) if delivered personally, at the time of delivery;
   (b) if sent by registered post, five (5) business days after the date of posting; and
   (c) if sent by email, at the time of transmission, provided that no delivery failure notification is received by the sender.

**11. GENERAL PROVISIONS**

11.1 This Contract constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, or agreements relating thereto.

11.2 No amendment or variation of this Contract shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the duly authorised representatives of both Parties.

11.3 No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right or remedy under this Contract shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise preclude any other or further exercise of any other right or remedy.
**13. ORDERING PROCEDURE**

13.1 The Buyer shall place orders for daily delivery by 16:00 hours on the day preceding the delivery date. Orders shall be placed through the Buyer's online ordering portal or, if the portal is unavailable, by email to the Supplier's designated order address.

13.2 Each order shall specify, at minimum: (a) the items and quantities required; (b) any quality or specification requirements not already set out in Schedule C; (c) the requested delivery window; and (d) any special handling instructions.

13.3 The Supplier shall confirm acceptance of each order by 18:00 hours on the day the order is placed. If the Supplier does not confirm acceptance by that time, the order shall be deemed accepted.

13.4 The Supplier may reject an order, in whole or in part, only where the Supplier is unable to source the requested Produce due to circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including crop failure, import restrictions, or force majeure events. The Supplier shall notify the Buyer of any rejection as soon as reasonably practicable and, in any event, no later than the order confirmation deadline.

13.5 Where an order is rejected or only partially accepted, the Buyer may place a replacement order for the affected items, and the Supplier shall use reasonable endeavours to fulfil such replacement order on the same delivery date or the next available daily delivery.

13.6 Standing orders for recurring daily quantities may be agreed in writing and shall be treated as orders placed in accordance with this Clause 13 for each day to which they relate, unless varied or cancelled by the Buyer in accordance with Clause 12.4.

**14. QUALITY STANDARDS AND INSPECTION**

The Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 specifies has_delivery_frequency as daily. Record status: current.

14.1 All Produce delivered shall conform to the specifications set out in Schedule C, including grade, size, ripeness, and packaging requirements.

14.2 The Supplier warrants that all Produce shall, at the time of delivery: (a) be fresh, sound, and fit for human consumption; (b) be free from pests, diseases, and contamination; (c) comply with all applicable food safety laws and regulations in Nigeria; and (d) have been handled and transported under appropriate temperature and hygiene conditions.

14.3 The Buyer or its authorised representative may inspect the Produce at the point of delivery. The Buyer may reject any Produce that does not conform to the requirements of this Contract, provided that the rejection is notified to the Supplier at the time of delivery or within two (2) hours thereafter.

14.4 Rejected Produce shall be removed by the Supplier at the Supplier's cost, and the Supplier shall replace the rejected Produce with conforming Produce on the next daily delivery unless the Buyer agrees otherwise.

14.5 Acceptance of any delivery shall not prejudice the Buyer's right to reject Produce later found to be defective or non-conforming, provided that the Buyer notifies the Supplier within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery.

14.6 The Supplier shall maintain records of quality checks, sourcing, and cold chain monitoring for a period of at least six (6) months from the date of each delivery, and shall make such records available to the Buyer upon reasonable request.

**15. PACKAGING AND LABELLING**

15.1 All Produce shall be packed in clean, food-grade packaging appropriate to the item, and shall be labelled with: (a) the item name; (b) the grade or specification; (c) the pack date; (d) the country of origin; and (e) the Supplier's name and batch code.
16.4 Prices may be reviewed quarterly by mutual agreement. Any adjustment shall take effect from the first day of the month following the month in which the parties agree the adjustment in writing. No retrospective price adjustments shall apply.

16.5 The Buyer may, by notice to the Supplier, deduct from any amount due to the Supplier: (a) any amounts properly due to the Buyer under this Contract; and (b) any penalties or liquidated damages properly levied under Clause 17.

**17. PENALTIES FOR LATE OR NON-DELIVERY**

17.1 If the Supplier fails to deliver any Produce on the due date, or delivers less than the ordered quantity, the Supplier shall pay to the Buyer a penalty calculated as follows:

Penalty = (Value of the undelivered or late Produce) × (Penalty Rate) × (Number of days of delay)

For the avoidance of doubt, the "Value of the undelivered or late Produce" means the Contract price for the Produce that was not delivered on time, or the Contract price for the shortfall, as applicable. The "Number of days of delay" means the number of days from and including the due date up to and including the date of actual delivery, or, if the Produce is never delivered, the date on which the Buyer cancels the relevant order or the delivery is deemed abandoned.

17.2 The penalty rate shall be two and one-half percent (2.5%) of the value of the undelivered or late Produce per day of delay. In the contract, the Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 has_penalty_rate of 2.5 percent per day is noted. Record status: current. This rate is current and shall apply for the duration of this Contract, from the effective date through the expiry date, unless varied by a written amendment signed by both parties.

17.3 By way of example, if a delivery of Produce valued at NGN 100,000 is delayed by three (3) days, the penalty shall be NGN 100,000 × 2.5% × 3 = NGN 7,500. The penalty shall be invoiced by the Buyer to the Supplier, or may be deducted by the Buyer from any sums due to the Supplier under this or any other contract.

17.4 The penalty under this Clause 17 shall be the Buyer's sole and exclusive remedy for late or non-delivery, other than the Buyer's right to terminate under Clause 12 or to obtain replacement Produce from a third party at the Supplier's cost under Clause 17.5. The parties acknowledge that the penalty is a genuine pre-estimate of the likely loss to the Buyer and is not a punishment.

17.5 If the Supplier fails to deliver on time, the Buyer may, after giving the Supplier twenty-four (24) hours' written notice, purchase replacement Produce from a third party. The Supplier shall pay to the Buyer the difference between the price paid by the Buyer for the replacement Produce and the price that would have been payable under this Contract, together with any reasonable costs of procurement. This right is in addition to the penalty under Clause 17.1, but the Buyer shall not be entitled to recover both the penalty and the price difference in respect of the same shortfall to the extent that this would result in double recovery.

17.6 The Supplier shall not be liable for any penalty under this Clause 17 to the extent that the delay or non-delivery is caused by a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 19, provided that the Supplier has complied with its notification obligations under that Clause.

**18. INVOICING AND RECORDS**

18.1 The Supplier shall keep, for a period of at least three (3) years from the date of each invoice, full and accurate records of all deliveries, invoices, and payments under this Contract. The Buyer or its authorised representative may, on reasonable notice, inspect such records during normal business hours.
**19. CONFIDENTIALITY**

19.1 Each party shall keep confidential and shall not, without the prior written consent of the other party, disclose to any third party any Confidential Information of the other party. "Confidential Information" means all information disclosed by one party to the other, whether before or after the date of this Contract, in writing, orally, or by any other means, which is marked as confidential or which a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including but not limited to: pricing, discounts, rebates, margins, recipes, specifications, customer lists, supplier lists, staffing information, and the terms of this Contract itself.

19.2 The obligations in Clause 19.1 shall not apply to any information which: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Clause; (b) was known to the receiving party before disclosure by the disclosing party; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without any obligation of confidentiality; or (d) is required to be disclosed by law, regulation, or any governmental or regulatory authority, provided that the receiving party gives the disclosing party prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent permitted by law) and cooperates reasonably with the disclosing party in seeking a protective order or other appropriate remedy.

19.3 Each party shall take reasonable precautions to protect the Confidential Information of the other party, and shall not use such Confidential Information except for the purpose of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Contract. Each party shall limit access to the other party's Confidential Information to those of its officers, employees, agents, and advisers who need such access for that purpose and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less stringent than those in this Clause 19.

19.4 The obligations in this Clause 19 shall survive the termination or expiry of this Contract for a period of five (5) years, except that any Confidential Information which constitutes a trade secret shall be kept confidential for so long as it remains a trade secret.

19.5 Nothing in this Clause 19 shall prevent either party from disclosing Confidential Information to its professional advisers (including legal, accounting, and tax advisers) on a need-to-know basis, or from making any disclosure required in connection with any dispute resolution proceedings under Clause 21.

**20. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBCONTRACTING**

20.1 The Supplier shall not assign, transfer, charge, or otherwise deal with this Contract or any of its rights or obligations under it, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the Buyer. The Buyer may withhold its consent in its absolute discretion.

20.2 The Buyer may assign, transfer, charge, or otherwise deal with this Contract or any of its rights or obligations under it, in whole or in part, without the consent of the Supplier, provided that the Buyer gives the Supplier not less than fourteen (14) days' written notice of such assignment.

20.3 The Supplier shall not subcontract any of its obligations under this Contract without the prior written consent of the Buyer. Any consent to subcontracting shall not relieve the Supplier of any of its obligations under this Contract, and the Supplier shall remain fully liable to the Buyer for the acts and omissions of any subcontractor as if they were the acts and omissions of the Supplier.
**21. FORCE MAJEURE**

21.1 Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Contract if such failure or delay results from a Force Majeure Event, provided that the affected party:

(a) notifies the other party in writing of the Force Majeure Event within seven (7) days of its occurrence, specifying the nature of the event, its likely duration, and the obligations affected; and

(b) uses reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance as soon as practicable.

21.2 For the purposes of this Contract, "Force Majeure Event" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected party, including but not limited to: acts of God; flood, drought, earthquake, or other natural disaster; epidemic or pandemic; fire or explosion; war or hostilities; terrorist attack; riot or civil commotion; strike, lockout, or other industrial action (other than by the affected party's own employees); import or export embargo; and any act, regulation, or order of any governmental or regulatory authority.

21.3 If a Force Majeure Event continues for a period of more than sixty (60) consecutive days, either party may terminate this Contract by giving not less than fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other party. Termination under this Clause 21.3 shall be without prejudice to the rights and obligations of the parties accrued prior to the date of termination.

21.4 The Supplier shall not be entitled to rely on a Force Majeure Event to excuse its failure to deliver Produce where the relevant Force Majeure Event could have been avoided by the Supplier maintaining adequate contingency arrangements, including (without limitation) alternative sources of supply within Nigeria.

(a) the Supplier commits a material breach of any of its obligations under this Contract and, in the case of a breach capable of remedy, fails to remedy such breach within fourteen (14) days of receiving written notice from the Buyer requiring it to do so;

1. REQUEST DESCRIPTION

We are requesting an additional weekly delivery on Saturdays for the Victoria Island and Ikoyi
outlets. Current contract provides for deliveries on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays only.
See attached delivery schedule from original contract.

2. RATIONALE / BUSINESS JUSTIFICATION

Saturday traffic at both outlets has increased by approx. 22% since March 2026 (see sales
reports from March – May). Weekend brunch service, introduced Q2, requires fresh produce
(e.g., leafy greens, tomatoes, fish) that cannot be stored over the weekend without quality
degradation. Current Friday deliveries are insufficient to cover Saturday and Sunday service.
Kitchen managers have reported occasional stock-outs of high-turnover items on Saturday
mornings, forcing last-minute purchases from local markets at higher prices.

3. PROPOSED CHANGE

CR-014 requests_additional_delivery of extra_weekly_delivery_on_saturdays. Record status: current. This would add
one (1) delivery slot every Saturday, arriving no later than 07:00 AM, to the same delivery
points as the existing Monday/Wednesday/Friday schedule. Estimated additional volume: 350 –
400 kg per Saturday across both outlets.

13.6 Standing orders for recurring daily quantities may be agreed in writing and shall be treated as orders placed in accordance with this Clause 13 for each day to which they relate, unless varied or cancelled by the Buyer in accordance with Clause 12.4.

**14. QUALITY STANDARDS AND INSPECTION**

The Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 specifies has_delivery_frequency as daily. Record status: current.

14.1 All Produce delivered shall conform to the specifications set out in Schedule C, including grade, size, ripeness, and packaging requirements.

14.3 The Buyer or its authorised representative may inspect the Produce at the point of delivery. The Buyer may reject any Produce that does not conform to the requirements of this Contract, provided that the rejection is notified to the Supplier at the time of delivery or within two (2) hours thereafter.

14.4 Rejected Produce shall be removed by the Supplier at the Supplier's cost, and the Supplier shall replace the rejected Produce with conforming Produce on the next daily delivery unless the Buyer agrees otherwise.

14.6 The Supplier shall maintain records of quality checks, sourcing, and cold chain monitoring for a period of at least six (6) months from the date of each delivery, and shall make such records available to the Buyer upon reasonable request.

**17. PENALTIES FOR LATE OR NON-DELIVERY**

17.1 If the Supplier fails to deliver any Produce on the due date, or delivers less than the ordered quantity, the Supplier shall pay to the Buyer a penalty calculated as follows:

Penalty = (Value of the undelivered or late Produce) × (Penalty Rate) × (Number of days of delay)

For the avoidance of doubt, the "Value of the undelivered or late Produce" means the Contract price for the Produce that was not delivered on time, or the Contract price for the shortfall, as applicable. The "Number of days of delay" means the number of days from and including the due date up to and including the date of actual delivery, or, if the Produce is never delivered, the date on which the Buyer cancels the relevant order or the delivery is deemed abandoned.

17.2 The penalty rate shall be two and one-half percent (2.5%) of the value of the undelivered or late Produce per day of delay. In the contract, the Main Supply Contract LFP-GS-2024-01 has_penalty_rate of 2.5 percent per day is noted. Record status: current. This rate is current and shall apply for the duration of this Contract, from the effective date through the expiry date, unless varied by a written amendment signed by both parties.

17.3 By way of example, if a delivery of Produce valued at NGN 100,000 is delayed by three (3) days, the penalty shall be NGN 100,000 × 2.5% × 3 = NGN 7,500. 17.4 The penalty under this Clause 17 shall be the Buyer's sole and exclusive remedy for late or non-delivery, other than the Buyer's right to terminate under Clause 12 or to obtain replacement Produce from a third party at the Supplier's cost under Clause 17.5. (a) notifies the other party in writing of the Force Majeure Event within seven (7) days of its occurrence, specifying the nature of the event, its likely duration, and the obligations affected; and

  from May and June. Some of those runs were not logged properly, so the baseline may be
  understated. Tolu is aware and will present the caveat alongside the numbers.

documents.title: Negotiation Log NL-2025-03
documents.content:
P.O. opened by referencing the Q4 2024 supply agreement (ref: SUP-2024-117) which had
a fixed price band for beef quarters (NGN 4,850 – 5,100 per kg) and frozen chicken
(NGN 3,400 – 3,650 per kg). A. Bello stated that the abattoir-side costs have moved
"significantly" since November – specifically cattle feed, diesel for cold chain, and
the new levies at Oko-Oba abattoir. Bello proposed a blanket increase of 18% across
both lines, but did not bring any cost breakdown sheet. P.O. noted that an 18% rise
would push beef kg price to approx NGN 5,720 – 6,020, which is beyond our internal
budget cap for the staff canteen contract. T. Ade flagged that the last increase
(July 2024) was only 8% and was tied to a documented feed-cost index.

P.O. asked Bello to come back with itemized cost evidence by 13-Jan. Bello said he
would "try" but hinted that other buyers (two hotels in Victoria Island) have already
accepted the 18%. No minutes were taken formally; this log is the only record.

OUTCOME: NO AGREEMENT – DISCUSSIONS OPEN. Next meeting scheduled for 13-Jan.

SUBJECT: DRAFT TERM SHEET – PRICE ADJUSTMENT CLAUSE

I. Obi joined to help draft a price adjustment clause that would allow a mid-term
revision if certain input costs move beyond a threshold. The discussion focused on
wording: should the trigger be a composite index (feed + diesel + transport) or
individual items? Bello preferred individual triggers; P.O. and M. Chukwu preferred
a composite to avoid "cherry-picking." No final text was agreed. Obi took notes and
said he would circulate a draft by 27-Jan.

Separately, T. Ade raised the issue of staffing – the canteen contract requires us
to provide 14 food handlers, but we are currently 3 short (two resigned in Dec; one
is on extended sick leave). Bello said his firm does not supply kitchen staff, only
raw materials, so this is outside his scope. P.O. noted that we may need to start a
separate recruitment drive or use an agency. This item was tabled for a later
internal meeting (see follow-up list at end).

ENTRY 005 | DATE: 03-FEB-2025 | INITIATED BY: P.O. / ATTENDED: A. BELLO, T. ADE, I. OBI (PHONE)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SUBJECT: PRICE REVISION – COUNTER-OFFER AND MOVEMENT

P.O. opened the meeting by restating the buyer's position: we cannot absorb a
15% increase on top of the abattoir levy (NGN 80/kg, effective 1-Mar) and the
transport rise. He proposed a counter-offer of 8% across all line items, with a
commitment to a 24-month volume guarantee (current monthly volume: approx. 4,200
kg of assorted cuts). Bello rejected 8% immediately, citing feed costs.

Bello then made a verbal counter-counter-offer: 12% across the board, but he
would include free delivery for the Ikeja route (previously charged separately
at NGN 15,000 per trip). He also said he could hold the 12% for 12 months,
subject to the price adjustment clause being drafted.

T. Ade asked for a breakdown of the 12% – which items in the basket are driving
the increase. Bello said feed is the main driver (he estimates +18% on maize and
soya since Oct-2024), followed by diesel. He did not have a written breakdown
with him but said he would email it by 5-Feb.

P.O. said he would take the 12% figure to management but flagged that the
buyer's internal approval threshold for a single-supplier increase is 10%.
Anything above that requires a written justification and a review of alternative
suppliers. Bello asked if we had a viable alternative; P.O. admitted we have not
received quotes from any other supplier since Dec-2024.

NL-2025-03 has_negotiation_outcome agreed_on_12_percent_increase. Record status: current.

I. Obi (phone) reminded both parties that any agreed percentage must be
documented in writing before it is binding. He noted that the current term sheet
is still marked "draft – subject to contract."

OUTCOME: SUPPLIER REVISED POSITION = 12% (VERBAL). BUYER COUNTER-OFFER = 8%.
NO AGREEMENT YET. BELLO TO EMAIL COST BREAKDOWN BY 05-FEB.

SUBJECT: COST BREAKDOWN EMAIL FROM BELLO (REF: BELLO/COST/2025-02-05)

Bello emailed a one-page breakdown (attached to the negotiation log file as
Annex A). Key figures:

- Feed (maize, soya, premix): 62% of total cost, up 18% vs Oct-2024 baseline
- Diesel (generator + delivery trucks): 18% of total cost, up 22%
- Labour (abattoir & cutting): 12% of total cost, up 5% (minimum wage review)
- Transport (third-party, Mile 12 – Ikeja): 8% of total cost, up 15%

Bello's note says: "The 12% across-the-board is my best offer. I cannot go
below that and still maintain the same spec (grade A, skin-on, bone-in)."

P.O. forwarded the email to management with a short cover note: "See attached.
Supplier's justification is feed-heavy. We are 2% above our approval threshold.
Recommend we either (a) accept 12% with a written commitment to renegotiate at
the 6-month mark, or (b) go back with a final 10% and see if he moves."

P.O. asked whether Bello would accept a 10% increase if the buyer committed

volume-guarantee question. No further counter-offer to be made this week.

advance payment request be reviewed by finance before any commitment.
